elements.text: The archive shall retain the submitted record, its source location and the sequence in which the reviewer encountered it. Each reconstruction shall retain links to the same immutable input. A successful conversion reports execution status; it does not certify that every value, relationship or note has been recovered.

A capture boundary encloses a page region and its explicit relationships. The boundary may include a caption, a body paragraph and a group of cells. A line drawn through a region is not, by itself, evidence that two values belong to different records.

The original spelling, capitalization and symbols remain part of the source evidence. If a source value appears unusual, the reviewer shall retain it and record a separate explanation. The conversion shall not replace a literal zero with a missing value or normalize a strict inequality into a non-strict one.
The trace follows the submitted item17 even when the note appears below.
NOTE 1 - The following note is explanatory body content. It remains associated with the section and is not a title, caption, running head or page footer.
Retention remains mandatory after a successful conversion.

Record order is distinct from physical drawing order. A visual paragraph can be assembled from many PDF text runs, while a single run may contain both a numerical value and a raised callout. The corresponding roles shall be reviewed without discarding the underlying glyphs.
capture window: The bounded interval used to select incoming records.
review token: An identifier used to preserve the source-to-result relationship.
record boundary: The visual region belonging to one submitted item.
retained evidence: The original text, image and relationships used for comparison.
NOTE 2 - Definitions use bold terms followed by colons. Their typography does not create a new section in the document hierarchy.

The three columns are a roster of independent fictional participants. There are no row-wise pairs between columns and no data header.
Table 1 records quantities at two observation scales. Units and relation signs belong to each value. The table notes and the page note below use different marker spaces.
The observation matrix is retained with its notes.
The source intentionally spells the status as "protcol pending". A corrected spelling would be a separate editorial operation.
Fractions and min operators are embedded within cells. Their presence does not turn the table into a stand-alone display equation.

A record within the retained band remains associated with its source. A boundary value is assigned according to the direction and strictness of the printed relation sign. The endpoint 1.16 occurs in adjacent conditions but belongs to one specified band.
The next physical page defines note 121 and continues Table 3.
When a record is divided across physical pages, its reference remains attached to the same logical item. The continuation begins with the remaining words of the
same sentence and does not create a new section merely because a running head intervenes.
The continued table does not introduce a second independent Table 3.
The archive retains both table fragments and the cross-page note.
The two expressions below are invented review metrics. Each right-aligned parenthesized number identifies one expression. Neither expression supplies an electrical engineering requirement.
In these fictional expressions, J is a review index and R is a normalized residual. The terms rms, base and the integer zero are distinct subscripts; they are not footnote markers.
The literal label "calbration" is preserved exactly as submitted.
Figure K.1 is an invented review decision path. Internal words and edge labels are figure content. Recovering an image is distinct from recovering its graph connections.
The internal threshold labels must not become body paragraphs in the reading sequence. Image preservation alone does not prove that the labels or edges were recognized.
Figure K.2 depicts a fictional archive fill ratio. The plotted curve, axis signs, units and inequality callouts belong to the same figure.
NOTE 3 - This explanatory note belongs to the figure discussion. It is not the figure caption and is not a running footer.
The final retained record includes the original source, the extraction, the unresolved differences and the reviewer decision. Repeated words do not authorize deletion of a body paragraph.
The root index is 3. The radical covers the full sum, and the exponent on each indexed term is also 3.
Identical marker letters do not establish that two notes are the same note.

Abstract: This fictional record describes how a laboratory archive retains submitted evidence, establishes source identity and records unresolved extraction differences. The review covers text roles, numerical symbols, mathematical expressions and the relationships between a submitted item and its source region.
Keywords: archive, source identity, traceability, table, review, evidence.
The cover identifies the issuing council. This abstract describes the record contents. Their physical adjacency does not establish that they form a single paragraph.
A true paragraph continuation is provided earlier in this fixture. Both cases use a physical page boundary and repeated page furniture, but their paragraph identities differ.
